text:
Evan: heads-uponboarding sample app hit an auth double-refresh loop on Android 14 emulators after ProGuard shrink. Repro+logs below; Authenticator runs twice and we issue duplicate refreshes.

Sara: can you paste logs + OkHttp config?

Evan: logs:
```
W/OkHttp: response for https://api.redwood.ai/token: code=401 message=Unauthorized
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=abc123)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete, new token saved
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=abc123)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete, but original call already retried -> 401 again
```
Client:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()
```

Mike: sounds like the interceptor attaches an old token while the authenticator refreshes, then triggers another request. ProGuard + Android scheduler shrank/inline timing which made the race worse.

Ashley: quick mitigations: 1) AuthInterceptor checks an atomic flag/mutex for in-flight refresh and avoids reattaching/stashing retries; 2) disable `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` on clients handling auth so OkHttp low-level retries don't overlap; 3) only trigger authenticator on responses with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

Mike: also avoid broad `synchronized` on Application; use a single-threaded CoroutineScope and `refreshMutex.withLock { ... }`.

Evan: tried mutex + disabling retryOnConnectionFailure for auth client. Much better; rare flakiness left but CI green. Post-change CI log:
```
[RUN] onboarding-sample - serial
I/Authenticator: starting token refresh (requestId=def456)
I/Authenticator: refresh complete
I/OkHttp: retried request with new token -> 200
[PASS] onboarding-sample
```

Sara: please update sample README and add an SDK docs note about interceptor vs authenticator ordering and Android patterns (Mutex/Coroutine, avoid double-refresh).

Ashley: found a missing ProGuard keep rule: obfuscation changed Token.equals/hashCode which broke AtomicReference checks. Add to proguard-rules.pro:
```
-keep class com.redwood.sdk.auth.Token { *; }
```

Evan: opened PR draft `devex/auth-mutex-disable-retry` with tests and README updates. CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/2199 (android-ci)

android-ci: Build 2199 succeeded (emulator API 34, 3/3 instrumentation tests passed) :white_check_mark:

Mike: follow-ups: 1) add e2e test simulating concurrent 401s; 2) mention ProGuard keep in SDK migration guide; 3) consider exposing `safeAuthClient()` helper in SDK that sets `.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` + recommended timeouts.

Evan: will open tickets and a small RFC for the helper. Thanks :thumbsup:
